text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tanker bleeds oil in Tokyo Bay: Japanese officials drastically reduce estimate of amount spilled in waterway.
- Cholesterol risk factors reassessed: New guidelines emphasize individual health elements rather than overall blood levels.
- Sun Life settles class-action suits: Landmark deal on 'vanishing premiums' could affect 400,000 customers in three provinces.
- Crestar to buy Grad & Walker for C$336 million: Friendly deal locks up founders' shares.
- U.K.'s Labour government taxes windfall profits: Former state-owned enterprises take 5.2 billion British pounds budget hit.
- TSE posts biggest gain of year.
- Sun Life to settle key premiums suit: Deal will be the first major settlement of vanishing premiums claims in Canada and shoould set industry standard.
- Markets applaud C$336 million Crestar, Grad deal.
- Scotiabank to pay C$260 million for control of Argentine bank.
